title: The partner access decision record has no operation, no field composition and no result vocabulary in any source
source: TSD P7 v2 T3.1/T-A.1/T6.1; FSD P7 v3; legacy RWB-E2-019; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41
section: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P7-001 to API-P7-008 and none is a partner access record; T3.1 gives decision_log_entry columns but no composition for this record
description: The story appends a partner access decision record in rwb_decision and serves two reads filtered to partner access entries. No source names the record path of rwb-access to rwb-decision, the partnerId and date-range filter of the two reads, the composition of actions and inputs_ref for this record, the result vocabulary (allowed or refused) behind final_call, the page-size bound parameter, the rwb-decision login name or the two index names. Each is written as a placeholder and read through the assumption in force.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 appendix T-A.1 endpoint inventory; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry fields; legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 5 and 14 name the decision codes and reasons only; Architecture v5 slide 14 names the decision ledger as an output without an operation
proposed: Fix the record path, the two query parameters, the entry composition, the result vocabulary, the page-size bound parameter and the index names in the rwb-decision contract baseline before the app build starts

title: The append path of a partner access record is read synchronously while Arch v5 names it as a consumed event
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 28 and 42 (event 08); TSD P7 v2 T5.3; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 5 and R-UNI-39
section: Architecture v5 slide 14 rwb-decision IN names DecisionRecorded from all 19 and no synchronous record operation; slide 28 collects the ledger within 5 minutes and applies strict mode only at points of no return
description: The slice requires that a record which cannot be appended refuses the access answer (MSG-P7-003, no session, incident under R-UNI-39), which needs an append on the answer path. Architecture v5 names the append as the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 consumed into the central ledger within five minutes, with strict confirmation only for debt transfer, write-off, auction sale and title transfer. The story therefore declares both: the record path called by rwb-access within the resolution, and the same record published on rwb.decision-record.v1 and deduplicated by the idempotency key. The conflict is recorded and the reading applied is ASM-B-P7-02-E2019-6.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (IN: events DecisionRecorded from all 19), slide 28 (collected centrally within 5 minutes, strict mode for points of no return), slide 42 event 08 (DecisionRecorded, producer all 19, consumers rwb-decision and rwb-reporting)
proposed: Confirm the dual path: the record path on the resolution for the fail-closed answer, and the topic for durability, the replay and the five-minute completeness target

title: The contact entry payload, the read shape, the final call of a passed check, the reason-code list, the message id set, the parameter names, the rule version label of R-LIT-03 and the login name have no source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1 to A2.5, A2.8 and A2.14 field catalog; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry, T3.2 LOV-DECISION, T-A.1 API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, T-A.2; legacy RWB-E2-022 sections 3, 4, 7, 9, 12, 14 and 17; Architecture v5 slides 28 and 41
description: Eight values of this story are not fixed by any source: (1) the payload field set of a contact entry, because no column of TSD P7 v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry holds the channel, the reason code or the requesting role, and the jsonb containers recommendation, actions and outcome are not described; (2) the request and answer shape of the two reads, because T-A.2 fixes the query as caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page and size and names DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry without their field set; (3) the final call of a send that passed the check, because the legacy story names a decision entry only for a contact stop and no source names a passed final call; (4) the reason-code list, because the legacy story names the causes in prose and no source enumerates a code list; (5) the message id set of this slice beyond the nine ids the legacy story and the P7 baseline already carry; (6) the parameter names and version labels of the page-size bound of the search and the 5-minute completeness target of the ingest; (7) the rule version label of R-LIT-03, the legacy giving a version label only for a universal rule; (8) the name of the per-service database login of DP-02.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and DF-DEC-028 to DF-DEC-031 with no channel, reason or role column; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006 request is 'Query: caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page, size' and its answers give no field set; legacy RWB-E2-022 AC3 names decision code X6 and final call contact refused and no criterion names a final call for a send that passed; legacy section 14 writes MSG-P6-001 with the placeholder {reason} and never enumerates the reasons; FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02 uses rule R-UNI-14 with rule version UNI-2026.11 and no source gives a version label for R-LIT-03; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives every service its own login and names none
area: P7 decision record: contact entry payload, read contract, reason codes, message set, parameters, service login
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the data steward, the P6 business analyst and the business owner
proposed: At the design review of wave 2 the solution architect, the data steward, the P6 business analyst and the business owner agree and approve, as reference data and as the OpenAPI of the service: the container of the channel, the reason code and the requesting role inside actions, the request and answer field set of the two reads, the final call of a passed check, the reason-code list and its labels, the message ids and texts of this slice, the parameter names and version labels of the page-size bound and the completeness target, the rule version labels, and the per-service login name; until then the story holds the assumed shape of ASM-B-P7-02-E2022-1 to ASM-B-P7-02-E2022-4

title: The legacy story names one decision entry only for the contact stop, while the contact check has five refusal causes and a send that passed the check
source: Legacy RWB-E2-022 AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC11 and section 4 step 4; RWB-P6-E2022-APP sections 2, 12.3 and BR13; Architecture v5 slide 28; FSD P7 v3 A2.2 and A2.5; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T-A.1
description: The sources disagree on what a contact decision records. Legacy RWB-E2-022 section 4 step 4 writes the decision log entry only on a failed check, and AC3 is the one criterion that names decision code X6 with final call contact refused, on the lost-contact cause; the other four refusal causes, X1 dispute or complaint, no consent on the channel, a legal hold and a withdrawn template, are named in AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC11 with no decision value at all. RWB-P6-E2022-APP section 12.3 declares DecisionRecorded for every refusal and for every send, and its BR13 makes the record mandatory for both. The slice therefore records all five refusals under decision code X6 and final call contact refused, with the cause distinguished by the reason code, and the send carries a final call that no source names. The legacy also wrote the entry once, in its own schema, while DP-03 writes a local record in the producer's schema and appends the central entry here; the two writes are read as one record, the local write being the one that blocks the action under R-UNI-39.
evidence: legacy RWB-E2-022 AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC11 and section 4 step 4; RWB-P6-E2022-APP section 2 reading of DP-03, section 12.3 and BR13; Architecture v5 slide 28 (a local record in the service schema plus the central collection); FSD P7 v3 A2.2 and A2.5; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T-A.1
area: P7 decision record: decision-code span of the contact check and the double write of DP-03
owner_role: Business owner, with the solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, and the P6 business analyst
proposed: Confirm at the wave 2 design review that one decision code X6 and one final call contact refused cover every refusal of the contact check with the reason code naming the cause, add the final call of a passed check to the service vocabulary as a reference row, and state in RWB-P6-E2022-APP and in this story that the local record of DP-03 is the write that blocks the send and the central append is the ledger copy under the completeness target

title: The dispatch decision record's payload, its field placement, the rule version label, the message id set, the parameter names, a panel id and the edge right of the two reads have no source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1 to A2.5, A2.10, A2.13 and A2.32 field catalog; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry, T3.2 LOV-DECISION, T-A.1 API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, T-A.2; RWB-P6-E2021-CON events published (the DecisionRecorded element); legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 4, 11, 12 and 14
description: Seven values of this story are not fixed by any source: (1) the payload field set of a D7.1 dispatch entry, because TSD P7 v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry has no column for the notice reference, the notice type, the hold reason, the delivery status or the notice period start date, and no source says whether they are new columns or jsonb members of actions and outcome; (2) the placement of those facts between actions and outcome and the shape of inputs_ref for a conduct-check record; (3) the rule version label carried by the letter rules R-LIT-04, R-LIT-05, R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09 and R-UNI-20, and whether those rules are rule_row rows of the registry at all; (4) the request and answer field set of the two reads, because T-A.2 API-P7-006 fixes the query as caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page and size with no notice-reference filter, and the T-A.2 answer names DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry without their field set; (5) the message id set of this slice, because MSG-P7-009 is named by the FSD P7 v3 exception flows and its text is written by no source; (6) the parameter names and version labels of the page-size bound and of the 5-minute ingest completeness target; (7) the panel or screen id that would show the dispatch record beside the notice, and the way the Decision log right and the caller's scope reach the two reads, because RWB-P6-E2021-CON fixes the record element as record reference, decision code, ruleId, ruleVersion, finalCall and decidedAt and no more.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and DF-DEC-028 to DF-DEC-031 with no notice, notice type, hold reason, delivery status or notice period column; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006 request is 'Query: caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page, size'; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 refuse with MSG-P7-009 naming ruleVersion and decisionCode, whose text no source writes; RWB-P6-E2021-CON events published declares DecisionRecorded as 'decision record reference, decision code, ruleId, ruleVersion, finalCall, decidedAt'; legacy RWB-E2-021 section 11 names DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 only; Architecture v5 slide 28 names the 5-minute completeness target as a value and no source names it as a parameter row; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 has no DP-08 in the pattern set of this story.
area: P7 decision record: dispatch entry payload, read contract, messages, panel, parameters, edge right and scope
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the data steward, the P6 business analyst and the business owner
proposed: At the design review of wave 2 the solution architect, the data steward, the P6 business analyst and the business owner agree and approve, as reference data and as the OpenAPI of the service: the dispatch columns of decision_log_entry (new columns or jsonb members of actions and outcome), the notice-reference filter and the answer field set of the read, the rule version label of the letter rules and their registry rows, the message ids and their texts, the panel id of the decision-log view, the parameter names and version labels of the page-size bound and the ingest target, and how the right and the scope reach the two reads at the edge; until then the story holds the assumed shape of ASM-B-P7-02-E2021-1, ASM-B-P7-02-E2021-2, ASM-B-P7-02-E2021-4, ASM-B-P7-02-E2021-5 and ASM-B-P7-02-E2021-6 and its nine criteria stand on that shape

title: The DP table adds platform and published dependencies, and two service baselines, that the metadata rows of the story do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table rows DP-01, DP-03, DP-05, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-13, DP-18 and DP-19; section R5.4 dependency classes; the metadata rows Depends on (build) = None and Contract dependencies = RWB-P6-E2021-CON; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1
section: Section 13 of the story, Pattern application; section 12.2; section 12.7; the metadata table
description: The DP rows the story applies add dependencies that are absent from its metadata: H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON from DP-03 (the decision-record library and rwb.decision-record.v1), H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON from DP-07 (the reference-data client library and the contract of rwb-case, which this story reads at the version in force carried by the record rather than by a call), H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON from DP-09 (the outbox and inbox library), H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON from DP-10 (the workflow kit that registers the Schedule owned by rwb-comms), H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON from DP-15 (the per-service Flyway sequence) and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON from DP-19 (the gateway-bff composite route). Two service baselines are needed and sit in no H row either: decision_log_entry with its append-only trigger tr_declog_append_only and its JOB-14 chain check at 02:00, and the rule registry rule_package, rule_package_version and rule_row read by rule id and version. The metadata names H None and C RWB-P6-E2021-CON only, so the platform and other-service dependencies are carried here and in ASM-B-P7-02-E2021-3 instead of in those two rows.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 'H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON', DP-07 'H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON', DP-09 'H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON', DP-10 'H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON', DP-11 'none (C from the legacy dependency)', DP-13 'none', DP-15 'H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON', DP-19 'H RWB-PLT-N001-CON'; ownership.json tables decision_log_entry, rule_package, rule_package_version and rule_row to P7; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 carries decision_log_entry and the append-only trigger; the story metadata rows Depends on (build) = None, Contract dependencies = RWB-P6-E2021-CON, Integration dependencies = None, External dependencies = None.
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the platform team and the rwb-case team
proposed: Carry the six platform H dependencies, the one published C dependency and the two service baselines in the dependency map as DP-added and baseline rows, keep Ready to start = Day 1 because every H is a platform CON story and every C is built against its published contract and fake, and correct the metadata rows at the next version of the story set

title: The record payload, the reference shapes and the correction final call of the RWB-E2-017 decision slice have no source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 4, 7 (AC2, AC3), 12 and 14; TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 slides 28 and 42; FSD P7 v3 A2.1 to A2.5
description: The sources fix the decision code D6.4, the final call SENT_FOR_SIGNATURE, the reason as override_reason, the template code and version and the document reference, but they name neither the final call of the correction entry, nor the shape of the document set reference, of the write-once reference and of the value pair identifiers, nor the payload field set the two records carry on rwb.decision-record.v1, nor the names of the two parameters (the page-size bound of the search and the completeness target of the ingest), nor the message id of MSG-P4-003 beyond its id.
evidence: Legacy AC2 names decision code D6.4 and override_reason and no final call; AC3 names final_call SENT_FOR_SIGNATURE and a document set without a reference shape; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives the columns of decision_log_entry only; Architecture v5 slide 42 names DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 without a schema; the legacy section 12 carries the operation names and no payload.
proposed: Read the payload from the published RWB-P5-E2017-CON record declaration, the correction final call and the decision code from the reference lists in force, and the two parameter names from the rwb-case parameters contract; write the placeholders until the P5 contract and the reference data settle them.

title: rwb-decision login, migration file and sequence, constraint and index names, standard-column Field IDs, the dictionary handover and the platform-contract carriage are not fixed by any source
source: TSD P7 v2 T3.0 and T3.1; LDM v8 fields sheet; Template and Rules v1 R7.1 and R7.3; R5 default rulings
description: Six values this slice has to state are absent from every source: the name of the per-service login of rwb-decision; the file name and the sequence number of the migration; the names of the constraints and indexes and the column order beyond the leading column; the Field IDs of the 7 standard columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.0; the way this story's field rows reach the one dictionary of rwb_source_data; and how the six platform contracts of the DP table are carried when the metadata H row is None and Ready to start is Day 1.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.0 lists the 7 standard columns with no Field ID; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and the LDM v8 fields sheet name no constraint and no index; no source names the rwb-decision login or the migration file, and D-RCV-28 fixes the naming rule only; the DP table rows RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON add H dependencies the metadata row of a secondary slice does not carry.
proposed: Build against the service baseline and its fakes, name the login in the text as the rwb-decision login (DP-02), fix the migration file and its sequence at merge under D-RCV-28, follow the platform naming convention for the constraints and the indexes with the read paths of section 13 as the leading columns, hand the field-row declaration to RWB-P1-E1001-APP as a build artefact proved by the conformance test, and carry the six platform contracts in the preconditions and in these rows instead of an H row.

title: LDM v8 states 18 fields for rule_row and a rule_test_case.package_version_id that its fields sheet does not define, and both name cross-schema foreign keys that DP-01 forbids
source: Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (entity sheet, fields sheet and relationships sheet); TSD P7 v2 T3.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01
description: The same document disagrees with itself on two points of this slice: its entity sheet states 18 fields for rule_row while its fields sheet lists 21 (DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015, DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054 and DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298), and its relationships sheet names rule_test_case.package_version_id, which its fields sheet does not define. Separately, TSD P7 v2 T3.3 and the relationships sheet declare approval.case_id as a foreign key to recovery_case and approval.delegation_limit_id as a foreign key to delegation_limit, whose owners are rwb_case (P3) and rwb_access (P4) in the target, so DP-01 forbids both keys.
evidence: LDM v8 entity sheet row rule_row states 18; the fields sheet lists the 21 rows above; the relationships sheet carries rule_test_case package_version_id but the fields sheet of rule_test_case stops at DF-REF-197. TSD P7 v2 T3.3 rows: approval case_id to recovery_case, approval delegation_limit_id to delegation_limit. Arch v5 slides 29, 41 and 45 and DP-01 forbid a cross-schema read and a cross-schema key.
proposed: The technical specification outranks the entity sheet on the column set and DP-01 outranks a cross-schema key: build rule_row with the 21 fields its fields sheet lists, create no rule_test_case.package_version_id, keep approval.case_id and approval.delegation_limit_id as values with no foreign key, and keep the five foreign keys of the schema inside rwb_decision; correct the LDM entity sheet, the relationships sheet and TSD P7 v2 T3.3 in their next versions.
